stage_name: Real hardware-in-the-loop: root-caused and fixed a real 2-byte stack buffer overflow in hal_identity_get_factory_base_mac() that silently corrupted this project's canonical GatewayId (FD-17) on any SOC_IEEE802154_SUPPORTED target (ESP32-C6, ESP32-H2) -- discovered because the connected device's real boot logs consistently showed mDNS/AP-SSID suffix 'fffe9f' instead of the naively-expected 'last 6 hex of the base MAC' ('9f0020'), an anomaly noticed but left open in the prior HIL round
note_on_commits: No new commit created; commits are only made on explicit user request. Layered on top of all prior uncommitted S5/S6 work and both prior HIL evidence files (HIL-persisted-state-stack-overflow-fix.json, HIL-flash-encryption-and-https-listener-verification.json) from this same session.
sequencing_note: This directly continues the still-open user goal from the prior HIL round ('generate a real CA+certificate, load it onto the device, verify the full end-to-end path'): before building a certificate with a DNS/URI SAN, the device's own runtime-computed GatewayId/mDNS-host value had to be trusted -- investigating the previously-unresolved 'fffe9f vs 9f0020' discrepancy (explicitly flagged as an open question in memory esp32c6-hardware-available.md) surfaced a real, independent memory-safety bug that had to be fixed first, since generating a certificate to match the *buggy* value would have been wrong (the bug is silent and would keep corrupting any newly-derived name on every future boot too).

root_cause.symptom: Every real boot of this device (both the original blank-eFuse boot and the later Flash-Encryption-enabled boot) logged 'SSID=zigbee-gateway-fffe9f' and 'mDNS started: https://zigbee-gateway-fffe9f.local', never the expected 'zigbee-gateway-9f0020' derived from the real factory base MAC 98:a3:16:9f:00:20 (confirmed via esptool chip_id's own 'BASE MAC' line).
root_cause.mechanism: hal_identity_get_factory_base_mac() (components/app_hal/hal_identity.c) called esp_efuse_mac_get_default(out) with `out` sized HAL_IDENTITY_BASE_MAC_LEN==6 bytes. esp_efuse_mac_get_default() is documented in ESP-IDF's own esp_mac.h ('@param mac base MAC address, length: 6 bytes/8 bytes... 8 bytes for EUI-64 (used for IEEE 802.15.4, if CONFIG_SOC_IEEE802154_SUPPORTED=y)') to require an 8-byte buffer on any IEEE802154-capable target. ESP32-C6 sets CONFIG_SOC_IEEE802154_SUPPORTED=y. Internally (esp_hw_support/mac_addr.c), esp_efuse_mac_get_default() reads the plain 6-byte factory MAC into mac[0..5], then calls insert_mac_ext_into_mac(mac): this saves mac[3..5] to a temp, overwrites mac[3..4] with the 2-byte MAC_EXT eFuse field ('ff:fe', a fixed IEEE 802.15.4 EUI-64 padding value), and writes the saved original mac[3..5] bytes to mac[5..7] via memcpy(&mac[5], mac_tmp, 3) -- i.e. it WRITES 3 BYTES STARTING AT INDEX 5, touching indices 5, 6, AND 7. Our caller-supplied buffer was only 6 bytes (valid indices 0-5), so indices 6 and 7 were a 2-byte out-of-bounds stack write on every single call. The in-bounds result left in mac[0..5] was {0x98,0xa3,0x16,0xff,0xfe,0x9f} -- OUI unchanged, but the real NIC bytes (9f,00,20) reduced to just one surviving byte (0x9f at index 5) with the constant EUI-64 padding (ff,fe) overwriting indices 3-4. GatewayId::format() of that corrupted 6-byte value is '98a316fffe9f'; its last 6 hex chars are 'fffe9f' -- an exact, byte-for-byte match to the observed anomaly, confirming the mechanism.
root_cause.confirmation_method: Derived and hand-verified the exact byte transformation against this device's own real chip_id output ('MAC: 98:a3:16:ff:fe:9f:00:20', 'BASE MAC: 98:a3:16:9f:00:20', 'MAC_EXT: ff:fe') by reading the real ESP-IDF v5.5 source for esp_efuse_mac_get_default()/insert_mac_ext_into_mac() in components/esp_hw_support/mac_addr.c inside the espressif/idf:release-v5.5 Docker image (not guessed from documentation alone), then confirmed the predicted corrected value against the real post-fix boot log.

impact: GatewayId (FD-17's 'canonical durable device identity') was silently wrong on any ESP32-C6/H2 build: instead of reflecting the true factory base MAC, its low 3 bytes were a near-constant 'ff:fe:<first NIC byte>' -- the two NIC bytes most likely to actually vary across sequentially-manufactured units (the last two, e.g. 00:20 here) were the ones being dropped by the out-of-bounds write, while the two bytes that survived into the visible suffix (ff:fe) are IDENTICAL on every ESP32-C6/H2 device in existence, since MAC_EXT's ff:fe padding is a fixed IEEE 802.15.4 EUI-64 convention, not per-device data.

Both the development provisioning AP SSID and the production mDNS hostname (build_provisioning_ap_ssid()/build_gateway_mdns_host(), both via build_prefixed_gateway_suffix_name()'s shared '<prefix>-<last6-hex>' convention) used this corrupted GatewayId, so a fleet of same-batch devices could have produced identical or near-identical SSIDs/mDNS names -- a real naming-collision risk on a shared LAN, not just a cosmetic one.

The production HTTPS certificate's URI SAN ('urn:zgw:<gateway_id>', built by build_gateway_uri_san()) would also have encoded the corrupted, low-entropy identity value had a certificate been generated before this fix -- directly relevant to the pending certificate-generation task this HIL round exists to unblock.

This was also a genuine, if narrow, memory-safety defect (an unconditional 2-byte out-of-bounds stack write on every single boot of every ESP32-C6/H2 unit this firmware has ever run on), independent of its identity-correctness impact.

This is a pre-existing HAL bug, not introduced this session -- present since hal_identity.c was first written; it had never been exercised on real IEEE802154-capable hardware before this HIL round (host/test builds use the mocked, unaffected branch).

fix.change: Replaced esp_efuse_mac_get_default(out) with esp_read_mac(out, ESP_MAC_EFUSE_FACTORY). esp_read_mac() with ESP_MAC_EFUSE_FACTORY reads the identical eFuse MAC_FACTORY field via the same internal get_efuse_factory_mac() helper esp_efuse_mac_get_default() itself calls first, but WITHOUT ever invoking insert_mac_ext_into_mac() -- confirmed via esp_mac.h's own enum comment for ESP_MAC_EFUSE_FACTORY ('MAC_FACTORY eFuse which was burned by Espressif in production (6 bytes)') and ESP_MAC_BASE ('Base MAC for that used for other MAC types (6 bytes)'), neither of which carries the conditional 8-byte IEEE802154 note that ESP_MAC_DEFAULT/ESP_MAC_CUSTOM do. This is a plain, always-6-byte, no-side-effect read exactly matching hal_identity.h's documented contract ('the factory base MAC... stable across reboot and factory reset').
fix.also_updated: hal_identity.h's doc comment for hal_identity_get_factory_base_mac(), and a new inline comment at the call site in hal_identity.c, both explaining the real finding so a future reader does not revert to esp_efuse_mac_get_default() without re-discovering this.
fix.other_call_sites_checked: grep confirmed hal_identity.c was the only call site of esp_efuse_mac_get_default() or esp_read_mac() anywhere in this project's own components/main code -- no other function needed the same fix.

tests_and_checks.method: Rebuilt with the same session-scoped HIL sdkconfig fragment as the prior round (CONFIG_SECURE_FLASH_ENC_ENABLED=y, CONFIG_SECURE_FLASH_ENCRYPTION_MODE_DEVELOPMENT=y, CONFIG_ZGW_PRODUCTION_PROFILE=y, CONFIG_PARTITION_TABLE_OFFSET=0x10000, CONFIG_PARTITION_TABLE_CUSTOM_FILENAME=partitions.production.csv) via `idf.py -B build-hil-tls build` inside espressif/idf:release-v5.5, then reflashed the already-Flash-Encrypted real device via `idf.py -B build-hil-tls -p /dev/ttyACM0 encrypted-flash` (the correct action learned from the prior round's recovery incident -- not a hand-copied write_flash command).
tests_and_checks.result: PASS. Build succeeded with zero new warnings. Flash succeeded (bootloader/app/partition-table/ota-data all rewritten with --encrypt, confirmed via the printed esptool command line).

tests_and_checks.method: Non-interactive pyserial capture (DTR/RTS hard-reset toggle, 20s read window) of /dev/ttyACM0 immediately after the reflash.
tests_and_checks.result: PASS. Log shows: 'Wi-Fi AP started (SSID=zigbee-gateway-9f0020, passphrase=...)' and 'mDNS started: https://zigbee-gateway-9f0020.local' -- the suffix now correctly matches the real factory base MAC's last 3 bytes (9f:00:20), exactly as predicted by the root-cause analysis. Boot proceeded cleanly through Wi-Fi AP, mDNS, and service_runtime start with zero panics; the production HTTPS listener's fail-closed certificate gate still correctly fired ('secure_storage: read key=\'tls_cert_cur\' status=1' -> 'refusing to start (fail closed)'), unaffected by this change (expected -- no certificate has been provisioned yet, that remains the next task).

environment_note: Real ESP32-C6 hardware at /dev/ttyACM0 (see memory esp32c6-hardware-available.md), accessed via `docker run --device=/dev/ttyACM0 espressif/idf:release-v5.5`. Flash Encryption (Development mode) has been permanently active on this chip since the prior HIL round; this round only reflashed application/bootloader/partition-table content, no further eFuse changes were made.
unresolved_blockers: The primary still-open goal from the prior HIL round remains open: generate a real private CA + device leaf certificate (DNS SAN = zigbee-gateway-9f0020.local, URI SAN = urn:zgw:98a3169f0020 -- both now confirmed correct against this fix) and load it onto the device's encrypted NVS storage to observe the HTTPS listener's positive path for the first time. This evidence file covers only the prerequisite identity-correctness fix, not that goal itself.
releaseability: This fix should ship as part of any future real release for ESP32-C6/H2 targets -- it corrects a genuine identity/memory-safety defect present in the codebase before this session, now proven and fixed against real hardware. Project has no live production deployment yet (see memory project-not-yet-in-production.md), so no migration/compatibility concern applies to changing the computed suffix.
